title: Replace application-enforced integrity with declared SQLite foreign keys and a strict loader
target_requirement: Deliver modern_schema.sql (SQLite DDL for ACCT_MASTER, CONT_MASTER, ORD_HEADER, ORD_LINE with declared PKs and FKs: contact/order -> account ON DELETE RESTRICT, line -> header ON DELETE CASCADE, DEL_FLG retired) plus migrated.py with load(conn, tables) that enables PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, applies the schema, inserts live legacy rows parents-first, and raises sqlite3.IntegrityError for orphans.
expected_behavior: Under PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON: orphan inserts into CONT_MASTER/ORD_HEADER/ORD_LINE fail; deleting an account with dependents fails (RESTRICT); deleting a header removes its lines (CASCADE); duplicate simple and composite PKs fail; load() inserts clean fixture data with correct counts, skips soft-deleted rows, fails loudly on a contact whose account was soft-deleted, and leaves the FK pragma enabled.
provenance: Synthetic; authored for LegacyCRM-Bench from Meridian CRM 4.2 spec (SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md §1, §2) and integrity_check.crms.
security_expectations: No weakening of the documented delete actions (account FKs must be RESTRICT, never CASCADE or defaulted; line FK must be CASCADE); dirty data must fail loudly rather than load silently; no DEL_FLG soft-delete backdoor in the modern schema; no network access.
failure_conditions: FKs missing, undeclared actions, or actions swapped; loader that swallows IntegrityError, loads soft-deleted rows, or forgets the foreign_keys pragma; extra or renamed tables; nondeterminism.
